name: dotstudio
description: Design calm, living screensavers and live wallpapers for your Mac with DotStudio.
long_description: Connects Claude to DotStudio (the macOS screensaver and live-wallpaper app). Claude reads DotStudio's style guide and your own brand guides, builds styles from DotStudio's scenes and looks, previews them as images, checks their GPU cost, and — only when you ask — sets them as your screensaver or live wallpaper. Needs DotStudio.app installed; the extension runs the server that ships inside it.

tools.name: get_started
tools.description: Orientation, guides to read, and this Mac's state.

tools.name: list_guides
tools.description: DotStudio's guides and the user's own.

tools.name: list_scenes
tools.description: The scenes and looks styles are built from.

tools.name: describe_scene
tools.description: A scene's params, colours, reactions and cost.

tools.name: create_style
tools.description: Add a style to the library.

tools.name: delete_style
tools.description: Remove a style the AI made (or one the user confirms).

tools.name: preview_style
tools.description: Render a style to a PNG or a contact sheet.

tools.name: import_style
tools.description: Add a style from a share file.

tools.name: list_displays
tools.description: Connected displays and what they show.

tools.name: set_wallpaper
tools.description: Change the live wallpaper (the user's Mac).

tools.name: film_status
tools.description: Can this Mac make photoreal film scenes?

tools.name: render_film_loop
tools.description: Render a seamless loop in the background.

prompts.name: design-a-screensaver
prompts.description: Design a screensaver from a mood, colours and a subject.
prompts.text: Design a DotStudio screensaver that feels ${arguments.mood}, in ${arguments.colours}, showing ${arguments.subject}. Call get_started first and follow DotStudio's style guide; preview and benchmark before showing me.

prompts.name: match-my-wallpaper
prompts.description: A screensaver that matches your desktop picture.
prompts.text: Make a DotStudio screensaver that belongs with my wallpaper: ${arguments.description}. Call get_started first and follow DotStudio's style guide.

prompts.name: brand-screensaver
prompts.description: A screensaver from a brand guide in DotStudio's guides folder.
prompts.text: Read the guide ${arguments.guide} and make a DotStudio screensaver in that brand's colours and tone. Call get_started first.
